headline_result_summary: Using propensity score matching across rural drinking water projects in 45 Indian villages, household participation—measured both actively via planning meeting attendance and passively via capital cost contribution (cash, labour, or materials)—has a statistically significant positive effect in the full sample on household water service improvements (PCA index difference = +0.749, t = 3.46 for meeting attendance; +1.04, t = 4.26 for capital cost contribution) and overall satisfaction (+0.105, t = 4.16; +0.355, t = 8.54). However, regional disaggregation shows these gains are concentrated in the Uttar Pradesh Hills (where overall participation and NGO capacity-building were strongest) and largely null at p < 0.05 in Northern and Southern Karnataka. Wealth-stratified matching shows no evidence of elite capture: poorest-quartile households gain substantial water service improvements from attending meetings (+1.680, t = 3.92), whereas richest-quartile households show a null water-improvement effect from meeting attendance (-0.0331, t = -0.09).
specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. PDF font-encoding glyph substitution: Throughout Tables 3, 4, and 5, Taylor & Francis PDF encoding renders minus signs ('-') as the digit '7' (e.g., Control mean '-0.676' is printed as '70.676', '-1.369' as '71.369', t-score '-2.04' as '72.04'), '<' as '5' ('Signiﬁcance 5 10 per cent'), and '>' as '4' ('Prob 4 w2'). Reading '70.676' literally as +70.676 instead of -0.676 would completely corrupt group means and signs. 2. Author prose typo on PDF p. 18: The text states 'the eﬀect of contributing towards capital cost has a positive and negative eﬀect on both water improvements and satisfaction'—an obvious typographical slip for 'positive and signiﬁcant eﬀect', as confirmed by Table 4 (Difference = +1.04, t = 4.26 and +0.355, t = 8.54) and the Abstract/Discussion. 3. Pooled vs. regional heterogeneity: While all four pooled ('All') PSM estimates in Table 4 are strongly positive (t = 3.46 to 8.54), disaggregated regional estimates for capital cost contribution on water improvements are null in every individual region (UP Hills t = 1.28, N. Karnataka t = 0.32, S. Karnataka t = 1.02), and meeting attendance on water improvements is significant at p < 0.05 only in UP Hills (t = 2.51; borderline t = 1.78 in N. Karnataka; null t = 0.70 in S. Karnataka). 4. Two-stage paper structure: Table 3 models determinants of participation (where SC/ST caste status and village size negatively predict capital contributions, and 'Quality of water before' is coded so higher values = POORER quality), whereas Tables 4-5 model the effects of participation on household water improvements (where higher PCA scores = BETTER water access/service).
study_design: Cross-sectional household survey across 45 randomly selected villages in two World Bank-assisted rural water supply and environmental sanitation projects (surveyed 1999-2000), analyzed using survey-weighted bivariate probit models (determinants of participation) and nearest-5-neighbors propensity score matching with replacement on common support (impacts of participation on household water outcomes).
unit_and_sample_size: Households across 45 villages in Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh, India. Total surveyed N = 1,523 households (valid N = 1,508 for meeting attendance; valid N = 1,408 for capital cost contribution; full-sample bivariate probit N = 1,158 [UP Hills N = 289, S. Karnataka N = 340, N. Karnataka N = 338]; propensity score matching trims low-end propensity scores for common support, exact post-trimming matched N not reported).
